rationale: Since dlc is a subset of lct, MA((act−dlc)/at) is nearly collinear with the archived "Liquidity-Backed Operating Strength" leg MA((act−lct)/at), making this a cosmetic component swap rather than a new mechanism test.

This is the already-evaluated "Liquid-Claim-Covered EBITDA Margin" with its first leg mechanically volatility-adjusted using the operator from another archive entry, so it is very likely near-collinear with prior results and offers no genuinely new economic question.

A defensible test of whether intangible-style SG&A intensity pays off specifically when working-capital efficiency is improving, though it is largely the intersection of two archived signals and the triple MIN will thin coverage and mechanically fight the shared-sale-denominator tension between margin and SG&A intensity.

Replacing the liability-intensity trend with its recent worst level is a coherent, diagnosis-motivated shift from change to persistent level, but the resulting leg is close to the low-leverage screens already tested (e.g., Solvent Profit Floor), limiting expected incremental information.

oiadp/MAX(oibdp,dp) equals 1−dp/oibdp for profitable firms, so it ranks capital/depreciation intensity rather than profitability as the hypothesis claims, and it is essentially the sign-mirrored version of the already-tested and weak "Capital-Consumption Liquidity Stress."

Trending current-debt concentration is a distinct maturity-structure channel not already in the archive (which tested only its level), though a 3-point annual TREND is noisy and the profitability leg is a standard ROA screen.
